content:
New folders should be created using gmail's web-mail in the browser. Creating them directly in Thunderbird for Android is not supported.

Once created, they will be available in Thunderbird for Android after refreshing its folder list.

To do this ...

  1. Open the side menu with your gmail folders displayed.
  2. Tap manage folders (bottom of the list).
  3. Tap the three dot ፧ menu > refresh folders.

Folder creation is a feature requested by the community of Mozilla connect. You can show support by voting for this at the link below.

https://connect.mozilla.org/t5/ideas/add-the-ability-to-create-imap-folders-on-android/idi-p/72777

content:
I may be misunderstanding. What your asking sounds like a pop3 account configuration where emails are stored locally on the device rather than the server.

TB does allow pop3 connections however it doesn't support local folder creation so you would have no means to move emails from inbox to an organised archive folder. The app also doesn't support backing up or exporting locally stored pop3 emails.

Your best option would be to archive the emails on a PC. A client such as Thunderbird desktop can download your emails over pop3, allowing them to be stored and archived locally on your computer.

OK, thanks for clearing this up for me. Apparently there is no email client available in an 'app" form for android (or Iphone-bsd linux) devices like Evolution for PC.

I used to have Thunderbird on my Linux machine, and for some reason I switched to Evolution as my PC email client (I still use Mozilla Firebird on all my Linux PCs and happy with Mozilla)..

The Evolution is configured and uses only the IMAP protocol to access a mail server. When I read and transfer an incoming message to local folder I guess Evolution not only copies the message to my PC, but at the same time "Deletes" - puts it into the trash icon, trash folder in the mail server. Yes, the message file is still retained in the mail server and counts towards the preset quota storage limit (16G for Gmail, I guess). Deleting "forever" files in the Waste bucket (Trash folder) finally frees up storage place.

So I was looking for something similar for smart phone.

No problem, I can do this on PC Evolution as long as I create a Gmail account for my wife and clean up her Inbox there. She will be able to see those moved messages on that particular PC that has her Evolution Gmail account.
